paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: This figure compares the error rate (one average minus test accuracy), computation cost, and GPU memory across our approach and baselines, for fine-tuning Llama-3-8B on ten NLP tasks with QAdapter.
model_annotation: The bar chart, titled "QAdapter," illustrates the computation cost associated with various fine-tuning methods. The horizontal axis contains the categorical methods, whose labels are rotated diagonally without an overarching axis title. The categories are positioned from left to right as "Full FT," "TAG," "Adapter," "MTL-FT," "QAdapter," and "Ours." The vertical axis represents the value, labeled "# FLOPs," and utilizes a logarithmic scale. The displayed value range spans from 10^18 to 10^20, with numeric tick labels and corresponding faint horizontal grid lines occurring at intervals of one power of 10. The chart features six individual vertical bars that generally follow a descending order in height from left to right, with the exception of the final category. The first five bars are colored solid orange. Among these, the "Full FT" bar is the tallest in the chart, reaching an approximate value of 6 x 10^19 FLOPs. The values then decrease for "TAG" (roughly 2 x 10^19 FLOPs), "Adapter" (slightly below TAG), and "MTL-FT" (approximately 4 x 10^18 FLOPs), leading to "QAdapter," which is the shortest bar overall with an approximate value of 2 x 10^18 FLOPs. The final bar, "Ours," has an approximate value of 2.2 x 10^18 FLOPs, making it slightly taller than "QAdapter." This final category is visually emphasized in two distinct ways: the bar is colored solid green to contrast with the orange bars, and its corresponding label on the horizontal axis is bolded.
